author: louisinger
body:
_This PR defines a new `ServiceWorkerWallet` implementing the `Wallet` interface. It uses a service worker files exported as `@arklabs/wallet-sdk/sw`_.

`src/sw/service.ts` defines a service worker file running a `BareWallet` instance and listening message from browser event listener. `ServiceWorkerWallet` sends requests defined in `src/sw/request.ts` to the service worker and handle the responses defined in `src/sw/response.ts`. 

Service worker is built and bundled via `esbuild`, the lib exports it as `@arklabs/wallet-sdk/sw`.

**Try it**

`test.html` is a simple webpage running a service worker wallet.

```bash
pnpm run build
```

```bash
pnpm run test:sw
```
 
 go to http://localhost:3030/

This pull request includes several changes to enhance the handling of user information in the backend and improve the shift proposal process. The most important changes include adding user ID handling in the `LogicGateController` and `ShiftProposalController`, ensuring the user ID matches the employee ID in shift proposals, and modifying role formatting in shift proposals.

Enhancements to user information handling:

* [`planner-backend/modules/logicGate/src/main/java/com/LIT/logicGate/controller/LogicGateController.java`](diffhunk://#diff-a70184ad2e754d301be352b2cfd018c4b21f540e9ddc77b4a00b48433f2c0581R118-R119): Added handling for `userId` in the `forwardGate` method, including setting the `X-User-Id` header if `userId` is present. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a70184ad2e754d301be352b2cfd018c4b21f540e9ddc77b4a00b48433f2c0581R118-R119) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a70184ad2e754d301be352b2cfd018c4b21f540e9ddc77b4a00b48433f2c0581R128-R131)
* [`planner-backend/modules/scheduler/src/main/java/com/LIT/scheduler/controller/ShiftProposalController.java`](diffhunk://#diff-3a115c8b42e663464046b2a5a6df767db1c721152e171f5972c1f324cc792251L31-R34): Updated the `createProposal` method to include `userId` in the request headers and pass it to the service layer.

Improvements to shift proposal process:

* [`planner-backend/modules/scheduler/src/main/java/com/LIT/scheduler/service/ShiftProposalService.java`](diffhunk://#diff-044d6f41c37664af81ac185b8be10d6d107de1c5cdd06b5c4b02984787f7e461L43-R56): Modified the `createProposal` method to ensure the `userId` matches the `employeeId` in the proposal and formatted the role to remove the `ROLE_` prefix if present. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-044d6f41c37664af81ac185b8be10d6d107de1c5cdd06b5c4b02984787f7e461L43-R56) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-044d6f41c37664af81ac185b8be10d6d107de1c5cdd06b5c4b02984787f7e461R68-R73)

Code cleanup:

* [`planner-backend/modules/scheduler/src/main/java/com/LIT/scheduler/service/ShiftService.java`](diffhunk://#diff-713d42cb22c67c71f914da9bdc7c942cb5b6ba350e6771302a9b3d6dd0b860fdL3-L4): Removed unused imports to clean up the code. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-713d42cb22c67c71f914da9bdc7c942cb5b6ba350e6771302a9b3d6dd0b860fdL3-L4) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-713d42cb22c67c71f914da9bdc7c942cb5b6ba350e6771302a9b3d6dd0b860fdL15)

Frontend adjustments:

author: iamdbychkov
body:
Hello!

Right now if you follow the instructions, CLI will create a file structure owned by root user and with write permission only for the owner of the file:

```shell
$ sudo docker run --rm -it -v ${PWD}:/docs squidfunk/mkdocs-material new .
INFO    -  Writing config file: ./mkdocs.yml
INFO    -  Writing initial docs: ./docs/index.md

$ ls -larth
total 16K
drwxrwxrwt 13 root     root     4.0K Mar 16 14:07 ..
-rw-r--r--  1 root     root       19 Mar 16 14:07 mkdocs.yml
drwxr-xr-x  2 root     root     4.0K Mar 16 14:07 docs
drwxr-xr-x  3 dbychkov dbychkov 4.0K Mar 16 14:07 .
```

which adds the necessity to change file's ownership as it is cannot be edited right away.


This can be avoided by using -u option in docker run command:

```shell
$ sudo docker run --rm -it -v ${PWD}:/docs -u $(id -u):$(id -g) squidfunk/mkdocs-material new .
INFO    -  Writing config file: ./mkdocs.yml
INFO    -  Writing initial docs: ./docs/index.md

$ ls -larth
total 16K
drwxrwxrwt 13 root     root     4.0K Mar 16 14:11 ..
-rw-r--r--  1 dbychkov dbychkov   19 Mar 16 14:11 mkdocs.yml
drwxr-xr-x  2 dbychkov dbychkov 4.0K Mar 16 14:11 docs
drwxr-xr-x  3 dbychkov dbychkov 4.0K Mar 16 14:11 .
```

Hence the proposed change

author: xyzboom
body:
Based on some of my recent findings, many Java developers new to Kotlin often confuse `obj as T` with `obj as T?`, especially when interacting with Java code. Accidentally writing `obj as T` instead of `obj as T?` may lead to unexpected NPEs. For this reason, I've added a warning block in this documentation.

You can see some example commits here:
[androidx-8e967e](https://github.com/androidx/androidx/commit/d0368b8bd00b91987340eaea3856a87c248e967e#diff-82fee78f32a586f9babd3fc0b7a548a1cb2977b9fecdf015b878a9c10cca2ee6L50)
[androidAPS-36b99e](https://github.com/nightscout/AndroidAPS/commit/22cad1a761b1955a628355d9006ceca34036b99e)
[androidAPS-49f0f1](https://github.com/nightscout/AndroidAPS/commit/407a7700a5714bcd2f521480179e14694049f0f1)
[androidAPS-f95b34](https://github.com/nightscout/AndroidAPS/commit/4c9052b29a166cb946fcc138afaa92458ff95b34)
[facebook-android-sdk-fd5a42](https://github.com/facebook/facebook-android-sdk/commit/8d4a2e19cbe9f75bb37eed76d7abd7c785fd5a42)

These fix commits demonstrate how easily people might mistakenly use `obj as T` instead of `obj as T?` during migration, which is precisely why I opened this PR.

author: adubrouski
body:
<!--
  Thank you for submitting a pull request!

  Please note that this template is not optional and all _ALL_ fields must be filled out, or your pull request may be rejected.

  Please do not delete this template.
  Please do remove this header to acknowledge this message.

  Please place an x, no spaces, in all [ ] that apply
-->

- [ ] This is a **bugfix**
- [x] This is a **feature**
- [ ] This is a **code refactor**
- [x] This is a **test update**
- [ ] This is a **docs update**
- [ ] This is a **metadata update**

### For Bugs and Features; did you add new tests?

Yes

### Motivation / Use-Case

Some applications use public paths (to avoid strong differences between dev and prod builds). I set it via output.publicPath, and it seems a bit inconvenient to me that the urls in the terminal are obtained without taking publicPath into account. These can be simple applications without routing, and you have to go to / and then manually add publicPath. I suggest outputting the url with publicPath if it is set statically, if it is determined on the fly - output without it.

Now, with config like this:

```javascript
output: {
  publicPath: "/my-public-path/",
}
```

We getting this:

```
<i> [webpack-dev-server] Project is running at:
<i> [webpack-dev-server] Loopback: http://localhost:8080/, http://[::1]:8080/
<i> [webpack-dev-server] On Your Network (IPv4): http://10.252.1.16:8080/
<i> [webpack-dev-server] Content not from webpack is served from '/home/user/Project/src' directory
<i> [webpack-dev-server] 404s will fallback to '/index.html'
```

My proposal is:

```
<i> [webpack-dev-server] Project is running at:
<i> [webpack-dev-server] Loopback: http://localhost:8080/my-public-path/, http://[::1]:8080/my-public-path/
<i> [webpack-dev-server] On Your Network (IPv4): http://10.252.1.16:8080/my-public-path/
<i> [webpack-dev-server] Content not from webpack is served from '/home/user/Project/src' directory
<i> [webpack-dev-server] 404s will fallback to '/index.html'
```

### Breaking Changes

No

### Additional Info

author: xyzboom
body:
Based on some of my recent findings, many Java developers new to Kotlin often confuse `obj as T` with `obj as T?`, especially when interacting with Java code. Accidentally writing `obj as T` instead of `obj as T?` may lead to unexpected NPEs. For this reason, I've added a warning block in this documentation.

You can see some example commits here:
[androidx-8e967e](https://github.com/androidx/androidx/commit/d0368b8bd00b91987340eaea3856a87c248e967e#diff-82fee78f32a586f9babd3fc0b7a548a1cb2977b9fecdf015b878a9c10cca2ee6L50)
[androidAPS-36b99e](https://github.com/nightscout/AndroidAPS/commit/22cad1a761b1955a628355d9006ceca34036b99e)
[androidAPS-49f0f1](https://github.com/nightscout/AndroidAPS/commit/407a7700a5714bcd2f521480179e14694049f0f1)
[androidAPS-f95b34](https://github.com/nightscout/AndroidAPS/commit/4c9052b29a166cb946fcc138afaa92458ff95b34)
[facebook-android-sdk-fd5a42](https://github.com/facebook/facebook-android-sdk/commit/8d4a2e19cbe9f75bb37eed76d7abd7c785fd5a42)

These fix commits demonstrate how easily people might mistakenly use `obj as T` instead of `obj as T?` during migration, which is precisely why I opened this PR.

author: mdqst
body:
I found a tiny typo in the following line of code:

```rust
                    panic!("Invalid input, lager than MODULUS")
```

The word **"lager"** should be **"larger"**. Here's the corrected version:

```rust
                    panic!("Invalid input, larger than MODULUS")
```

While "lager" is great for a cold drink, it's not quite what we need here.
The message is clearly comparing numbers, so "larger" is the way to go.
Let’s save the beer for later and make sure the logic is on point!

author: ostrzyciel
body: This tidies up exception handling in decoders and encoders, reducing the chance that some NPE, array-out-of-bounds, class-cast, or whatever exception slips out. There would be nothing inherently *wrong* with that, as it's all unchecked exceptions anyway, but such exceptions are not very informative to users. By catching and re-throwing them, we can make it clearer why a failure has occurred.
